podcast.title: Early Career as Folk Singer
podcast.body: Beck started his career as a "weirdo, slacker, folk singer," touring from coffee house to coffee house, often traveling by Greyhound bus. "After starting out as a weirdo, slacker, folk singer, touring from coffee house to coffee house on a Greyhound bus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Self-Described "Loser" Persona
podcast.body: Beck described himself as a "loser" at the time his hit song "Loser" gained popularity, reinforcing his unconventional image. "soon everybody was singing and wrapping along with this Beck guy, a self-described loser."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transition to Drum Machine Experimentation
podcast.body: After returning to LA, Beck began experimenting with a newly acquired drum machine, which led to his breakthrough sound. "Beck Hanson returned to LA and started playing with a newly acquired drum machine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unique Genre Blending
podcast.body: His music was noted for defying easy categorization, being "not folk, that's not rap, it's not hip-hop, it's not rock, it's just Beck." "So it's not folk that's not rap, it's not hip-hop, it's not rock, it's just Beck."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
